The buggy method is `com.google.javascript.jscomp.ProcessCommonJSModules.ProcessCommonJsModulesCallback.visitScript(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`.

Static evidence is direct:

- In [`ProcessCommonJSModules`](absolute/path unavailable), `visitScript` always calls `emitOptionalModuleExportsOverride(script, moduleName)` at line 191.
- `emitOptionalModuleExportsOverride` always appends:
  ```java
  if (moduleName.module$exports) {
    moduleName = moduleName.module$exports;
  }
  ```
- Every failing test has the same pattern: the expected CommonJS rewrite is correct, but this extra trailing conditional is appended even when the source only uses `exports.foo = ...` or no exports at all.

That matches the failures exactly:
- `exports.test = 1` incorrectly becomes `var module$foo$bar={test:1}; ...module$exports...`
- `var name = require('name');` incorrectly gets the same tail
- AMD-to-CJS also gets the same tail after the correct transform

So the root cause is not in `CommandLineRunner` or AMD transform ordering. It is that `visitScript` emits the `module.exports` override unconditionally instead of only when the file actually uses `module.exports`.

Dynamic verification was attempted on this method, but the debugger reported the nominated lines as unreached, so the conclusion here is based on static code plus the very consistent failure signature.
